title: Customer Request Elasticity Index (CREI) and adaptive roadmap slots
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Introduce a quantitative index (CREI) that normalizes and prioritizes incoming customer requests across revenue, immediate business impact, operational risk, and engineering effort. CREI will feed an adaptive roadmap slots system: a small, reserved set of short-cycle slots that can be dynamically allocated to requests that exceed a CREI threshold. Goal: reduce ad-hoc escalations, make tradeoffs auditable, and shorten time-to-decision for top-account asks.
background: We currently rely on ad-hoc PM judgment and several semi-manual scorecards to prioritize strategic customer requests. This causes long decision loops for enterprise escalations and inconsistent commitments across cycles. Sales and CS frequently escalate due to opaque queue positions. Engineering cites context-switching and unclear cost signals when requests are shoehorned into sprints.
proposed_solution: Design and implement the Customer Request Elasticity Index (CREI), a composite score combining: (a) ARR exposure weight, (b) number of affected customers, (c) latency to revenue impact (time sensitivity), (d) operational risk score, and (e) estimated engineering effort. CREI normalization will produce a 0-100 score; requests above a configured threshold (pilot = 60) are eligible for allocation into a 6-slot adaptive roadmap buffer each six-week cycle. Implement CREI computation in the intake form, surface it in the roadmap console, and automate routing to a 'CREI buffer' lane for PM/Eng review. Pilot with six strategic accounts over two cycles.
acceptance_criteria: CREI calculation implemented and stored on intake records
Roadmap console shows CREI score and CREI buffer lane with visual indicators
Automated rules place eligible requests into CREI buffer when score >= 60
Pilot with 6 accounts completed and outcomes documented (decision time, committed vs deferred)
Stakeholder sign-off (Sales, CS, Platform Eng) on CREI weights and threshold
Telemetry: median intake-to-decision time reduced by >=30% for pilot cohort
tasks: Implement CREI calculation in intake API (Backend)
Add CREI field and buffer lane to roadmap console (Frontend)
Create admin UI to tune weights and threshold (Ops)
Instrument dashboards: intake volume, CREI distribution, decision latency (Observability)
Run pilot: onboard 6 accounts, collect feedback, iterate weights
notes: We intentionally weight ARR highest to reflect commercial gravity for top accounts, but will add a penalty for long-running technical debt items to avoid bias toward low-effort but high-revenue asks.
Engineering effort term is inverted (lower effort increases CREI) to favor quick wins; this can be toggled in admin UI.
Buffer slot sizing (6 per cycle) is conservative; we will model utilization after two cycles and adjust to observed demand elasticity.
